name: ScrollFloat-TS-TW
title: Scroll Float
description: A huge word and a smaller caption assemble letter by letter as the block scrolls into view, each character dropping from below, stretched tall, then snapping to its final shape.
use: A landing page manifesto or big brand headline should assemble as the reader scrolls.
avoid: Content above the fold: it only animates once the block scrolls into view.
a11y: The copy is real text, but characters start invisible and there is no reduced-motion fallback. (keyboard: n-a, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A very large black-weight white word holds the centre of a black stage, with a smaller muted grey caption beneath it. Characters are tightly tracked in a clean geometric sans.
behaves: Scrolling brings each character up in turn from below, tall and faint, then snaps it to normal width and full opacity so the words settle into a line. Scrolling back lifts the letters away again.
customise: The text is passed as children; duration, easing, start and end scroll points, stagger and class names are props. Character splitting is fixed.
weight: light: A scroll timeline over one line of character spans; nothing renders per frame.
demo: "StashUI" over "every character floats into place", with a SCROLL DOWN hint above.
issues: The caption is cut off at the bottom edge in frames 3 and 4.
polishWhy: Strong scale and a springy settle; the giant word crowds a tight crop.
